cases.prompt: Use $review-pr to review the base-to-head change. Do not post comments.

files.base:
name: ci
on: [push]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npm test
files.head:
name: ci
on: [push]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npm test || true

expectations: The scope classifier activates silent-pass-verification even though the diff is small.
The review identifies that a failing test command now exits successfully and can let broken code pass CI.
Any finding is anchored to the changed workflow line and survives structured finding validation.
The review remains read-only and does not post comments or change git state.

cases.prompt: Use $review-pr to review the base-to-head change. Do not post comments.

files.base: export const sum = (left, right) => left + right

import test from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { sum } from '../src/math.js'
test('adds positive values', () => assert.equal(sum(1, 1), 2))
files.head:
import test from 'node:test'
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import { sum } from '../src/math.js'
test('adds positive values', () => assert.equal(sum(1, 1), 2))
test('adds zero values', () => assert.equal(sum(0, 0), 0))

expectations: An ordinary feature-test assertion does not activate silent-pass-verification by itself.
The review reports no actionable finding when the added assertion is valid and no other defect survives verification.
The coverage ledger may mention regression coverage but does not manufacture a CI or test-harness risk.
The review remains read-only and does not post comments or change git state.
